findings.source: collector.py lines 44-48 and 172-174 (utf-8-sig decode + ast.parse(str)); selector is a byte ERE
findings.text: ast.parse on a decoded str ignores PEP 263 coding cookies, and a byte-level ERE cannot see identifiers written through non-ASCII-transparent source codecs (for example utf-7). This is inherited from the original selector and is outside the bounded claim (no whole-corpus Python security proof). At 746789a the 398 tree .py contain 0 coding cookies and 0 non-UTF-8 files (reviewer P02). A future reuse could refuse any in-root .py carrying a non-UTF-8 coding cookie.

DirEntry.is_symlink() does not flag Windows junctions; a junction under a root would be followed (over-inclusion or RecursionError, not a silent drop). Reviewer found 18 directories and 0 junctions under the roots in this worktree. Optional: also refuse os.path.isjunction / reparse points.

findings.source: collector.py lines 99/144 (working decodes every enumerated .py) vs 172 (commit decodes selected only)
findings.text: Working mode fails closed on any non-UTF-8 .py in the roots even when it does not match the selector; commit mode only on selected files. Conservative asymmetry; no file is dropped either way.

\b is a GNU ERE extension resolved by the Git binary (git version 2.47.0.windows.1 here). Original and new selection share the same engine, so semantics are identical by construction; the reviewer Python-re cross-check agreed on 746789a (25/398).
